findings.title: Other subgroup methods still dereference a possibly-null model supplier
findings.body: The fix in getSubGroupsCount acknowledges that modelSupplier.get() can return null when a cached group has been deleted concurrently. However, getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, and the overloads at lines 262 and 268, still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If one of these methods is invoked for a cached group whose delegate no longer exists, it will throw a NullPointerException instead of handling the missing group consistently. This leaves the same concurrent-deletion race able to produce 500 errors in other subgroup query paths.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount can now return null and expose null subGroupCount in responses
findings.body: When the delegate group cannot be loaded, getSubGroupsCount now returns null. Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass this value directly to GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount, so admin API responses can contain a null subgroup count for a cached group that has disappeared. This is a different contract from a numeric count and may confuse clients or cause NullPointerExceptions in consumers that unbox the Long. The code path also does not register cache invalidation, unlike getDelegateForUpdate, so it does not actively clear the stale cached entry.

findings.title: Concurrency test does not wait for the reader thread and can miss failures
findings.body: The test starts a background thread that records exceptions, then deletes groups, sets deletedAll, and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty. There is no join, latch, or timeout, so the assertion can run before the reader thread finishes its current request, and exceptions added after the assertion are missed. The test also does not verify that any read actually overlapped with the deletes. If the delete loop throws, deletedAll may never be set, leaving the reader thread running after the test. Use a join/CountDownLatch, ensure at least one concurrent read occurred, and stop the thread reliably in a finally block.
